requirements.description: Four workers with independent identity, role, prompt, model/session, mode, timeout/retry and health; account binding shown as deterministic or pooled

requirements.description: Claude Manager analyses, plans, decomposes and assigns; plan is validated; planning is persisted and resumable

requirements.description: Automatic execution through the bridge with a stable idempotency key and no duplicate turn after a restart
requirements.acceptance: A resumed execution re-uses its key inside the replay window and fails as outcome_unknown after it
requirements.evidence: pytest tests/test_workforce_execution.py 7 passed + tests/test_workforce_bus.py 1 passed (local integration: FAKE bridge over real HTTP/SSE, real PostgreSQL; the bus test adds real RabbitMQ and a real worker process that is killed and replaced): each worker uses only its own session and conversation id; key wf-task:{task}:attempt:{n} -> acc-{execution}-r0; a resumed execution re-sends the same key inside the replay window and the fake records ONE turn; after the window it fails as outcome_unknown and nothing is sent again; duplicate commands/events change nothing. A real Arena Local Bridge was NOT used (WF-20)

requirements.description: Disabled workers receive no new tasks; the Manager redistributes; manual reassignment
requirements.acceptance: Tasks planned for a disabled worker go to an eligible one or wait with a reason; reassignment is audited
requirements.evidence: pytest tests/test_workforce_modes.py 8 passed (mock tier + FAKE bridge): a task planned for a disabled worker goes to an eligible worker with the skills (recorded as redistributed) or waits with a stated reason until one is enabled; nothing is sent for a disabled worker; manual reassignment is audited and refused when it would lose work; Automatic, Human-Assisted and Disabled workers finish one objective together; one task at a time per worker

requirements.description: Review: approve, reject, request revision or escalate to a human; never accepted on HTTP 200; original responses and revisions kept
requirements.acceptance: Every attempt is an immutable version; a criterion marked unmet can never be approved by the Manager
requirements.evidence: pytest tests/test_workforce_review.py 27 passed (MOCK Manager + FAKE bridge): HTTP 200 only creates a submission; every attempt is an immutable version with its own review; approve/revise/reject/escalate; an approval with an unmet criterion is overridden; revision limit, instruction-like text, unreadable verdict and an unavailable Manager leave the result with a person; a critical task is completed only by a human approval of exactly the reviewed version (frozen payload; a mismatch is not honoured). Review quality with a real model NOT verified (WF-21)

requirements.description: One consolidated result that separates verified facts, worker proposals, unverified claims, failed, incomplete and human-approved items
requirements.acceptance: Classes are computed from persisted evidence, not from model text; mock results are labelled
requirements.evidence: pytest tests/test_workforce_report.py 26 passed (mock tier): six classes computed from recorded rows (18-case rule table + end-to-end objective with one result per reachable class); the Manager's summary is stored as model text and cannot change a class (asserted with a summary that claims everything is verified); mock results, mock review, mock plan and mock summary are labelled in JSON and Markdown; one report version per state. The class 'verified' is reachable only by a machine check, which nothing produces until WF-14 — asserted empty for text-only runs

requirements.description: Failure recovery: bridge or account unavailable, timeout, invalid response, rate limit, worker/queue/database interruption, with bounded retries and Human-Assisted fallback
requirements.acceptance: Each failure is classified, bounded and leaves the task in a recoverable state
requirements.evidence: pytest tests/test_workforce_recovery.py 36 passed + tests/test_workforce_bus.py 1 passed (local integration, FAKE bridge, MOCK Manager): 19-row failure policy table; bridge unreachable (bounded retries, then a person or FAILED), account/session unavailable (not retried), revoked terms, task timeout, empty/tool-call/garbage responses, rate limit with Retry-After, circuit breaker; a lost message is re-enqueued at worker start; redelivered commands and events are idempotent; a scheduling round that raises half-way is rolled back whole; a killed worker process is replaced and the objective completes with one turn sent. Database and broker outages were simulated at the application level here, not by stopping the servers

requirements.description: Security: RBAC, tenant isolation, audit, secret redaction, untrusted-output isolation, frozen approval payloads
